title: Read a logistic regression off two Gaussians, then try naive Bayes
brief: Turn fitted means, a shared covariance and priors into the weights, log odds and boundary of the equivalent logistic regression, then fit Gaussian and word-count naive Bayes and score documents.
hints: w = solve(cov, means[1] - means[0]). Use np.linalg.solve instead of forming the inverse. The bias is log(priors[1] / priors[0]) - 0.5 * (means[0] + means[1]) @ w.
The log odds is the log posterior of class 1 minus the log posterior of class 0. Take both columns from gda_log_posterior.
In one dimension w is (mu1 - mu0) / var and b is log(pi1 / pi0) - w * (mu0 + mu1) / 2. The boundary is where w * x + b = 0, so x = -b / w.

For each class, X[y == k].mean(axis=0) and X[y == k].var(axis=0) give the per-feature mean and variance. np.var divides by the class count by default, which is what you want. Apply np.maximum(variance, var_floor).
For the word model, sum the count rows of a class first, then add alpha to every word, then divide by that smoothed total. The log of the result is one row of log_theta.

A document's score for a class is counts @ log_theta[k] + log_priors[k]. For all classes at once that is X @ log_theta.T + log_priors, an (n, K) array. Subtract log_sum_exp(joint, axis=1) as a column.
